name: Question 4
worked_solution:
Let's construct our matrix:

- The index $3$ in ${J}_{3}(-8)$ means that we have a $3\times 3$ matrix.

- The value $-8$ in ${J}_{3}(-8)$ means that we have $-8$'s on the main diagonal.

- Also, we must have $1$'s on the superdiagonal (the diagonal above the main one).

Given that all the other entries must be zero, our Jordan block is

$$
{J}_{3}(-8)=[\begin{aligned}-8 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -8 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

Let's construct our matrix:

  • The index 3 in J3(−8) means that we have a 3×3 matrix.

  • The value −8 in J3(−8) means that we have −8's on the main diagonal.

  • Also, we must have 1's on the superdiagonal (the diagonal above the main one).

Given that all the other entries must be zero, our Jordan block is

J3(−8)=[−8100−8100−8].
